name: Hell and Eternal Punishment
path: Eschatology: The Doctrine of Last Things

objectives.text: Recall that the Bible teaches God is holy and good and will punish sin
Name hell as the place the Bible describes where the wicked are punished away from the presence of the Lord
Explain why sin against God is serious using verses that describe His holiness and the wages of sin
Identify passages where Jesus Himself warned about hell
Explain the tradition's teaching that hell is the just penalty for sin against a holy God
Compare the descriptions of eternal life and eternal punishment in Jesus' teaching about the sheep and the goats
Explain from Scripture how Christ delivers His people from the wrath to come by bearing God's judgment in their place
Explain how Paul and Jude connect the reality of coming judgment to urgent and compassionate persuasion of others with the gospel
Analyze the biblical images of hell such as fire, outer darkness, the undying worm, and the lake of fire
Distinguish the biblical terms Sheol, Hades, and Gehenna and how each is used in its context
Interpret the phrases everlasting punishment and eternal destruction by comparing them with parallel phrases in their context
Explain the biblical teaching that punishment in hell differs in degree according to knowledge and deeds
Analyze how the tradition connects the justice of eternal punishment to the holiness and majesty of the God who is sinned against
Construct a careful biblical case for the reality of hell from Old and New Testament texts read in context
Evaluate annihilationism against the biblical language of conscious and unending punishment
Evaluate universalism against biblical texts that teach two final destinies
Formulate a sober and respectful response to common objections to the justice of eternal punishment
Compose a theological essay synthesizing how divine justice and mercy are both displayed in the final separation of the righteous and the wicked

changes: Rewrote Jude references in chapter:verse form (Jude 1:7, Jude 1:13, Jude 1:22-23) so they resolve. Kept the core competencies from the older list, reworded with observable verbs, and dropped vague items such as the general final judgment objective, which belongs to the sibling sub-topic on resurrection and judgment. Added objectives on Christ bearing wrath for His people, the terms Sheol, Hades, and Gehenna, degrees of punishment, and evaluating universalism separately from annihilationism. Recast the gospel urgency item as explaining the biblical basis for persuasion rather than a felt response. Added Westminster Shorter Catechism Q19, Heidelberg Catechism Q37 and Q44, and Belgic Confession 37 where they state the doctrine, and named the Westminster Confession of Faith in full.
